answer: Consider an agent marketplace brokering timber shipments. Sybil resistance comes from a puzzle-priced admission toll. On a calm day the toll is trivial; when a gale of fake signups arrives to bid on freight, difficulty spikes, so each puppet pays fresh compute per identity, a relic trader admitted earlier pays nothing more, and an honest newcomer pays once. Puzzle solutions are non-transferable and verified in microseconds, so flooding the order book costs the attacker full CPU price per fake agent, with no bulk discount, while real brokers keep bidding at normal cost.
